title.narrative: NDICI STABILITY THREATS/FPI01/ACT-63011/Organised Crime and Counter-Terrorism

description.narrative: Due to the ever-increasing growing connections between organised criminal groups and terrorist networks and the need for more coordinated responses to the two interlinked phenomena, this action aims to respond to two priorities of the Multi-Annual Indicative Plan (MIP) in an integrated way: supporting counterterrorism, including preventing and countering violent extremism and radicalisation (priority 4), and fighting global and trans-regional aspects of organised crime (priority 6). The action is the result of an internal rationalisation process, aiming to reduce the number of existing discrete and loosely connected interventions and to develop a smaller number of larger, more coherent global actions in order to reduce duplication, increase efficiency and facilitate international cooperation between geographical regions in a truly global response. The action will therefore seek to complement, and in many cases, eventually replace, the existing actions within the Global Illicit Flows Programme, and FPI¿s `CT facilities¿.The overall objective of this action is to face emerging global threats and challenges from organised crime and terrorism, while continuing to respect human rights, gender equality and the rule of law. Five components are planned, each aiming to address a separate dimension of the evolving terrorism-organised crime threat. These are:Component 1 - Criminal Justice: The specific objective of this component is to contribute to strengthening criminal justice responses to countering Terrorism and Organised Crime. This component will provide a flexible support to the entire criminal justice chain in selected partner countries and to regional organisations and networks; will improve international cooperation and information sharing for the two phenomena; and will offer on demand policy support to partners, in order to deliver on the EU¿s security dialogues, strategies and related commitments.Component 2 ¿ Multi-route anti-trafficking integrated cooperation platform: The specific objective of this component is to support the disruption of illicit trafficking via containers, civil, general aviation and maritime routes. This will be achieved by building capacity for control and tracking of vessels, aircraft, and containers and by supporting intelligence exchange and analysis related to these potential trafficking modalities.Component 3 (EU Global Facility on Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing): The specific objective of this action is to support partner countries worldwide in strengthening their policy, legislative and regulatory frameworks and building their analytical and institutional capacity to close loopholes used by criminals to launder illicit proceeds or finance terrorist activities, in line with EU directives on anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT), UN Security Council resolutions and recommendations of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF). This component builds on the strong experience of the existing EU Global Facility on Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing. Component 4 ¿ Prevention and Countering of Violent Extremism (P/CVE): The specific objective of this component is to enhance P/CVE efforts in partner countries by strengthening regional and international cooperation focusing on emerging threats with a focus on preventing child/youth recruitment.
